title: Morgan Stanley sees Sensex at 1.05 lakh in bull case by December 2027; base target at 95,000 - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Morgan Stanley’s latest base case assumes robust domestic growth, steady global growth, a resolution of the India-US trade deal and Brent crude below $100 a barrel.

Morgan Stanley has pegged the BSE Sensex at 95,000 by December 2027 in its base-case scenario, implying an upside of 16 per cent from its November 12, 2026 reference level of 81,911. In its bull-case scenario, the brokerage sees the benchmark rising to 1,05,000, while its bear case places the index at 68,000.

The base case carries a 50 per cent probability, while the bull and bear scenarios have probabilities of 30 per cent and 20 per cent, respectively. The probability-weighted outcome is 90,750.

The brokerage’s November 2026 outlook compares with its November 2025 projection, when it had set a base-case target of 95,000 for December 2026 and a bull-case target of 1,07,000. At the time, it had also moved its earlier bull-case projection of 1,00,000 from June 2026 to 1,07,000 by December 2026. The latest outlook therefore retains the 95,000 base-case level but extends the target horizon by a year, while placing the bull-case level at 1,05,000.

Morgan Stanley’s latest base case assumes robust domestic growth, steady global growth, a resolution of the India-US trade deal and Brent crude below $100 a barrel. It also factors in another 75 basis points of policy rate increases and a positive liquidity environment. The brokerage projects Sensex earnings to compound at 18.1 per cent through FY29.

Its bull case assumes oil prices remain below $75 a barrel, easing supply-side pressures and reforms that support economic and market flows. In the bear case, crude staying above $100 a barrel for several months, monetary tightening by the Reserve Bank of India and a meaningful global slowdown could weigh on equities.

Morgan Stanley favours domestic cyclicals over defensives and externally oriented sectors, maintaining an overweight stance on financials, consumer discretionary and industrials.
